latest_rss.title: AI Will Deepen Divide Between the PRC’s Two Economies
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




The economic consequences of artificial intelligence (AI) may be especially marked in the People’s Republic of China (PRC) because they will feature a major positive supply shock and negative demand shock in an economy that already presents too much of both.



The 15th Five-Year Plan places AI in pole position of the “modern industrial eco-system,” comprising all manner of manufacturing, technology, infrastructure, and control over global supply chains.



The very policies that are powering the industrial side of the PRC economy are exacerbating structural weaknesses and flaws in the much larger part of the economy where excessive debt, low productivity, high unemployment, and fiscal and financial failing are becoming more deeply entrenched.

latest_rss.title: Russia’s Bipolar Economy Opening Door to Disaster Ahead
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




President Vladimir Putin’s Russia has two economies. The burgeoning military-industrial one continues to support his invasion of Ukraine despite sanctions, and the troubled civilian sector is at best stagnating and near free fall.



Analyses that lump the two together obscure this divide and allow the Kremlin to present a positive picture while Russia’s critics present one overstating how close its economy is to collapse.



More seriously, this divide points to disaster ahead for Russia because, in most other countries, innovation now comes from the civilian sector rather than the state. This pattern will leave Russia behind, and Putin is trying to compensate for it through espionage and sabotage.
